title: Earth Wasn't Made of Space Junk from Far Away, Scientists Say
summary: Imagine building a sandcastle. Where did the sand come from? Right next to you, or from a beach far, far away? For years, scientists thought some of Earth's building blocks came from the outer solar system — way out past Jupiter. That's because Earth has water, and water is easier to find far from the sun. But a new study says: nope. Almost everything that made Earth came from the inner solar system, right around where Earth sits today. The team, Paolo Sossi and Dan Bower at ETH Zurich, looked at atoms in meteorites. Atoms come in slightly different weights called isotopes (say it: EYE-so-topes). Think of them like siblings — same family, different sizes. By comparing many of these atom "siblings" at once — ten different kinds — they found Earth is made of just one material recipe. Less than 2 percent came from far away. Maybe none at all. "We were truly astonished," Bower said. So why does this matter? It means Earth grew up in a calm neighborhood. And it means the water in our oceans was probably here all along — not delivered from far away. Jupiter may have acted like a wall, keeping outer material out. Next, scientists want to test this idea even more.
why_it_matters: Knowing where Earth's water came from helps us understand why our planet can support life — including your family, your school, and you.

background_read: ETH Zurich, where the two scientists work, is a large science university in Switzerland.
Meteorites are space rocks that survive the trip through the air and land on Earth; scientists study them like fossils to learn how planets formed.
Scientists think the solar system — the sun plus all the planets — formed about 4.6 billion years ago from a spinning cloud of dust and gas.
Article_Structure: WHO: Scientists Paolo Sossi and Dan Bower at ETH Zurich, who studied atoms inside meteorites
WHAT: A new study says almost all of Earth was built from material in the inner solar system, with less than 2 percent coming from far away
WHERE: The inner solar system, near where Earth sits today, with Jupiter possibly acting as a barrier
WHY: It suggests Earth's water was here from the start and that Earth grew in a calm neighborhood of space

perspectives.description: The study gives strong evidence that Earth was built mostly from nearby material — a big surprise that changes the old story.
Other researchers say more tests are needed before everyone agrees, so the debate isn't over yet.
If planets like Earth make their own water instead of catching it from far away, then other watery worlds might be more common than people thought.
